newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer-dlr/mark normalisation to end soon.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer-dlr/mark normalisation to end soon.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that he expected the normalisation of the mark's exchange rate against the dollar to end soon, a spokesman for the central bank confirmed.
Tietmeyer made the comments earlier today on the fringes of an official gathering in Bonn. The spokesman confirmed the comments in answer to Reuter enquiries.

The spokesman, who had verified Tietmeyer's comments with the Bundesbank president, quoted Tietmeyer as saying, "The normalisation of the mark against the dollar will reach an end soon. The mark will remain a strong currency."
The dollar, which has risen about 10 pfennigs against the mark since the start of the year, fell on Tietmeyer's initial comments.

But it recovered in late afternoon, as rumours circulated in financial markets that Tietmeyer's remarks had been misinterpreted. Another variation of the rumour said Tietmeyer would hold a news conference later today to retract the comment.
The Bundesbank generally does not comment on rumours of this type.
